name: Dalian Wanda Group
desc: Chinese private conglomerate in commercial property, cinemas, hotels, sports media and entertainment, controlled by the Wang family.
sponsorships: FIFA sponsor for World Cups up to 2030 (deal signed 2016); owns Infront Sports & Media
markets: Commercial property and Wanda Plazas across China; cinemas, hotels and sports media internationally, including Infront in Europe.
rationale: Already a FIFA top-tier sponsor and owner of Infront Sports; F1 would fit its sports, leisure and hospitality interests.

name: miHoYo (HoYoverse)
desc: Shanghai video game developer behind Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero, published globally as HoYoverse.
capacity_detail: Main business revenue CNY 27.34bn (about USD 3.8bn) in 2022 (zh Wikipedia infobox; converted at about 7.1 CNY/USD)
markets: Games played worldwide via HoYoverse, with large audiences in China, Japan, Korea, North America and Europe.
rationale: Global gaming brand with young international audience; rivals Tencent and PUBG Mobile already use F1 for brand reach.

name: Tiens Group
desc: Chinese private group selling dietary supplements and wellness products through multi-level marketing networks in many countries.
markets: China plus direct-selling networks in Russia, Europe, Africa and Asia, with distributors in Germany and Uganda.
rationale: Distributor-incentive business that uses travel and spectacle; F1 hospitality could reward top distributors across its international network.

name: Godrej & Boyce (Godrej Enterprises Group)
desc: Indian private manufacturer of aerospace parts, appliances, Godrej Interio furniture, locks, security and engineering equipment.
capacity_detail: Revenue INR 11,800 crore (about USD 1.3bn) in 2021-22 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Mainly India, with engineering and aerospace work for international customers in defence, energy and automotive sectors.
rationale: Precision-engineering and aerospace capability gives an F1 technology story; consumer brands Interio and Appliances need premium visibility.

name: Mother Dairy
desc: Indian dairy company selling milk and dairy products under the Mother Dairy brand, mainly in Delhi NCR.
capacity_detail: Revenue over INR 17,000 crore (about USD 1.9bn), year not stated (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: India, especially Delhi NCR, which took over 65% of sales in 2025.
rationale: Large consumer food brand, but domestic and state-controlled; an F1 link would only suit an Indian race or campaign.

name: Fulton Hogan
desc: New Zealand infrastructure contractor building roads, water and transport infrastructure and producing asphalt and precast concrete.
capacity_detail: Revenue $6.80bn in 2025, presumably NZ$ (about USD 3.9bn at 0.57) (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: New Zealand and Australia, with over 6,500 staff in New Zealand and over 4,000 in Australia.
rationale: Large B2B contractor in Australasia; Melbourne Grand Prix hospitality could serve government and infrastructure clients.

name: Aurecon
desc: Australian engineering, design and advisory firm working on infrastructure, property, energy, water and defence projects.
capacity_detail: Revenue AUD 1.06bn (about USD 0.69bn) in 2020 (Wikipedia infobox); owned in trust for employees
markets: Australia and New Zealand plus international work; formed in 2009 from Australian and South African engineering firms.
rationale: Engineering consultancy competing for talent and infrastructure clients; F1 engineering story fits its design and innovation positioning.

name: Intrepid Travel
desc: Australian tour operator running small-group adventure and responsible travel trips led by local guides worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue AUD 626m (about USD 410m), year not stated (Wikipedia infobox); majority owned by co-founders and staff
markets: Trips across all continents, with offices in Melbourne, London, Toronto and Seattle selling to global travellers.
rationale: Global consumer travel brand; F1 race-trip packages could fit, though its responsible-travel image may limit motorsport appeal.

name: Ishida
desc: Japanese family-owned maker of weighing and packaging machinery and retail POS systems for food producers and retailers.
capacity_detail: Consolidated sales JPY 159.3bn (about USD 1.06bn) in the year to March 2024 (ja Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Japan plus subsidiaries in Europe, Brazil, Malaysia, China, Thailand, Canada, Korea, Vietnam, Indonesia and India.
rationale: Precision weighing technology sold to global food manufacturers; F1 hospitality and engineering story suit B2B customer relations.

name: Proterial
desc: Japanese maker of specialty steels and high-performance materials, formerly Hitachi Metals, now owned by Bain Capital.
capacity_detail: Consolidated revenue JPY 942.7bn (about USD 6.3bn) in the year to March 2022 (ja Wikipedia infobox); 100% owned by BCJ-52
markets: Japan-based materials maker with over 21,000 staff and subsidiaries including US medical-device component makers.
rationale: Japan's leading specialty steel maker with high-performance materials; an F1 technical partnership fits its automotive materials business.

name: Jamco
desc: Japanese maker of aircraft interiors and aircraft parts, delisted in July 2025 after Bain Capital took control.
capacity_detail: Revenue JPY 80.4bn (about USD 0.54bn) in the year to March 2026 (ja Wikipedia infobox); delisted July 2025 under Bain Capital
markets: Aircraft interiors and parts for aviation customers, with subsidiaries in Japan and the United States (Jamco America).
rationale: B2B aerospace interiors supplier; F1 would serve only client hospitality, so a modest fit.

name: Crown Worldwide Group
desc: Hong Kong-based private group providing relocation, logistics, records management, fine art and workspace services in 53 countries.
markets: Over 270 locations in 53 countries, with regional headquarters in Hong Kong, New York and London.
rationale: Moves executives and fine art for multinationals worldwide; F1 hospitality would suit its corporate mobility and premium logistics clients.

name: OPPO
desc: Chinese private smartphone maker selling OPPO, OnePlus and realme devices in more than 60 markets worldwide.
capacity_detail: Official smartphone partner of the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Super Cup, renewed in 2024 for three seasons (to 2026-27)
sponsorships: UEFA Champions League official partner (renewed 2024 for three seasons); Roland-Garros partner from 2019; FC Barcelona sponsor from 2015
markets: Smartphones sold in more than 60 markets across Asia, Europe, the Middle East, Latin America and Africa.
rationale: Already spends on UEFA Champions League; rival smartphone brands use F1, and its global premium push suits F1 audiences.

name: Foodstuffs North Island
desc: New Zealand retailers' co-operative running supermarket and grocery store banners across the North Island.
capacity_detail: Revenue NZ$9.23bn (about USD 5.3bn at 0.57) in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: North Island of New Zealand; with Foodstuffs South Island it holds an estimated 53% of NZ grocery.
rationale: Large domestic grocer with heavy consumer marketing, but no international reach, so an F1 deal would make limited sense.

name: LGMG (Lingong Heavy Machinery)
industry: mining trucks and aerial work platforms
desc: Chinese maker of wide-body mining trucks, aerial work platforms, forklifts and construction machinery parts.
capacity_detail: Listed on the Hurun Global Unicorn Index (valuation USD 1bn+) for 2023, 2024 and 2025, per the company's own page
markets: Sales across China, Europe, North America, Japan, Korea, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and Africa; plant in Mexico.
rationale: Expanding machinery exporter selling to global rental firms; F1 hospitality could support dealer and rental-customer relationships abroad.
